anim-home.vocabulary:
The app's open/close animation vocabulary, measured by reading the CSS. All line numbers are in styles.css unless marked otherwise.

(1) HOME family (global keyframes, usable anywhere)
- hm-rise, 6371: translateY(15px) + opacity 0 -> none. Home intro uses it at .5s cubic-bezier(.22,.9,.32,1) backwards (6389). The tab-change restage uses .22s with the same ease (6394).
- hm-rise-fab, 6376: keeps translateX(-50%) in both keyframes, plus translateY(18px) scale(.86) -> rest. Used at .55s (6396). This is the ready-made keyframe for anything centred with left:50% plus translateX(-50%).
- hm-bloom, 6370: opacity 0 -> 1. Used for the backdrop at 1.15s and 1.7s.
- hm-tab-pop, 7725: scale 1 -> .93 -> 1 over 180ms cubic-bezier(.3,.8,.4,1). The press dip on a tab.
- hm-dot-pop, 9324: staggered 0/60/120ms, 340ms cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1). Touch only (hover:none). The ⋯ dots.
- hm-glint: the ring around the open project card.

(2) PHONE HINGE family, queue 612 (he picked it). Keyframes only exist inside @media (max-width:700px) at 9091.
- fm-hinge-corner, 9097: perspective(1400px) rotateX(-78deg) rotateZ(-3deg) -> 0, 320ms cubic-bezier(.18,.85,.28,1.02) both. Used by #ctx-menu.ctx-hinge. contextmenu.js sets transform-origin to the corner.
- fm-hinge-up, 9116: perspective(1400px) translateY(100%) rotateX(-58deg) -> 0, 360ms, same ease. Used by #add-sheet.open with origin 50% 100%. It sets transition:none so it doesn't double-animate (queue 706).
- fm-hinge-panel, 9125: perspective(1600px) rotateX(-42deg) translateY(14px) -> 0, 360ms, same ease. Used by #fx-browser.fxb-sheet: the shallower swing meant for large or full-height panels.

(3) PC POP family, queue 548. Keyframes only exist inside @media (min-width:701px) at 8878.
- pop-grow / pop-grow-down, 8936/8941: translate(var(--pop-dx,0), var(--pop-dy,0) ±6px) scale(.86) opacity 0 -> 1, 190ms cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.3,1.08) both. Used by .pop-card through js/popfrom.js (FM.popFrom), with a comic tail.
- pop-flip, 8954: rotateX(-82deg) -> 0, 340ms cubic-bezier(.18,.85,.28,1.02). The notepad only.
- cv-grow, 7665: scale(.82) translate(6px,-10px) -> 1. The editor canvas-settings cog card, 160ms.

(4) SCREEN TRANSITIONS
- fm-push-in/out/lead and fm-pop-in/out: 380ms (var --fm-push-ms). Push-in eases with cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.28,1); pop uses cubic-bezier(0,0,.2,1).
- The home -> editor slide.

(5) OTHER TRANSITIONS AND ONE-OFFS
- Settings side panel: transform translateX(-100%) -> 0 over .24s cubic-bezier(.22,.8,.3,1), plus a scrim background fade over .24s (5709-5718).
- sb-panel-in/out and sb-item-in/out (747-753), the editor side bars: 190ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) in. Out is 140ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,1,1), described as 'exit is decisive, not the entrance reversed'.
- vb-hint-in: 120ms ease-out.
- cog-turn: 280ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.3,1). Only the editor's .ico cog turns; the home cog (#hm-settings-btn) has none.
- touch-pop, fm-pausebloom and ld-in: small feedback pieces.

(6) CONVENTIONS THE CODE REPEATS
- Every animation has a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override.
- To restart a class-driven animation, the class is removed, then `void el.offsetWidth`, then the class is added.
- A class-driven entrance must be added after layout measurement (contextmenu.js 124-141).
- Close is usually instant: ctx-menu, dialogs and overlays just get .hidden. The only animated close on home is the Settings panel. The code's stated rule for exits is a fast 90-140ms, no stagger.

menus.name: Settings panel (home cog) — also opened from the editor at js/app.js:5739/5746
menus.where: Opened by js/settings.js:770-781 (FM.settings.open). The code rebuilds .set-scrim/.set-panel, then at line 778 runs `requestAnimationFrame(() => scrim.classList.add('open'))`. Cog button: js/home.js:2596-2601 (#hm-settings-btn). Close: js/settings.js:782-788. CSS: styles.css:5709-5718
menus.evidence: THIS IS A BUG: the slide-in exists in the CSS but never plays. Probe probes/p_settings2.js (a document-level transitionrun/animationstart listener, 450ms after the click) recorded no transitionrun for .set-panel or .set-scrim when opening. I got the same result in 3 runs: phone light, phone dark and PC 1280. Closing does record 'transitionrun set-panel transform' and 'transitionrun set-scrim background-color', a 240ms slide-out. A per-frame sample (probes/settings.js) shows the panel already at matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0) on the first frame after the click (t=14ms), with getAnimations() empty. Screenshots settings-open-light-0.png and -60.png show the panel fully there. CAUSE: open() inserts brand-new nodes, and the .open class is added in the same rAF that runs before their first style resolution, so the browser never sees the translateX(-100%) starting state. PROOF: probes/settings3.js adds `void document.querySelector('.set-panel').offsetWidth` straight after the click. With that, both transitionrun events fire, and transitionend arrives 246ms later. SEPARATELY, IN LIGHT MODE: on the light home the panel is the dark glass colour, background rgba(12,28,37,.82) with text rgb(233,244,247). theme-glass.css has no html[data-home="light"] .set-panel rule. This is the 'settings menu stays light in light mode' issue Ezra raised.
menus.proposed_animation: No new animation is needed; the existing one just has to play. It is the .24s cubic-bezier(.22,.8,.3,1) translateX slide plus the .24s scrim fade. Fix in js/settings.js:778: force a reflow before the class goes on, e.g. `void panel.offsetWidth; requestAnimationFrame(() => { if (scrim) scrim.classList.add('open'); });`, or use a double rAF. anim-editor.vocabulary:
Everything below was measured at 380x800 and 1280x900 with tools/shot.py. Scratch folder: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ezrasmith-Claude-FreeMotion/fde0eeaf-7d73-45b8-9f83-7761553e344d/scratchpad/audit/anim-editor/. The probe helpers are in lib.js, the tests in t/*.js, and the raw results in out/<test>-<width>.txt. Each probe clicks or calls the real opener, then reads document.getAnimations() for the menu's subtree in the same task, along with the computed animation-name and transition. It then samples opacity, transform and rect at 0, 40, 100, 200 and 400ms.

CAVEAT: the load average was 190–250 because other auditors were running at the same time, so the sampled timings are coarse (headless frames were delayed). The verdicts do not rely on them: getAnimations() and the declared animation/transition are deterministic.

The editor has 5 motion languages.

(1) PHONE "HINGE FAMILY" — his pick, queue 612, styles.css:9073-9136, gated to @media (max-width:700px). Each surface swings about the edge it comes from.
- fm-hinge-corner, 320ms cubic-bezier(.18,.85,.28,1.02) both, on #ctx-menu.ctx-hinge. contextmenu.js sets transform-origin to the corner the clamp chose, and adds the class only after measuring.
- fm-hinge-up, 360ms, on #add-sheet.open, origin 50% 100%. It closes with the base `transition: transform .22s ease` slide (mobile.js:393 closeAdd).
- fm-hinge-panel, 360ms, perspective(1600px) rotateX(-42deg) translateY(14px). Only #fx-browser.fxb-sheet uses it.

(2) PC "POP FAMILY" — queue 548, styles.css:8877-8963, gated to @media (min-width:701px). Placed by js/popfrom.js with a comic .pop-tail, and the button is lifted out of the blur (.pop-src).
- pop-grow, 190ms cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.3,1.08) both, from opacity 0, +6px, scale(.86). The keyframe carries --pop-dx/--pop-dy, which fall back to 0.
- pop-grow-down, the same, from -6px.
- pop-flip, 340ms cubic-bezier(.18,.85,.28,1.02), rotateX(-82deg). Notes only: the "unique" animation he asked for.
- cv-grow, 160ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.3,1), for canvas settings (styles.css:7651).
- In this family ONLY THE OPEN IS ANIMATED; every close cuts to display:none or remove at t=0.

(3) SIDE RAILS, both layouts (styles.css:747-788, driven by js/app.js:5911-5946 setSideBar):
- In: sb-panel-in / sb-panel-inL clip-path reveal, 190ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1). Controls follow with sb-item-in / sb-item-inL, 200ms cubic-bezier(.34,1.4,.64,1), staggered 26ms from a 40ms delay.
- Out: sb-panel-out 140ms and sb-item-out 90ms. The JS hides the rail on animationend.
- Lesson recorded at styles.css:770: use fill `backwards`, not `both`, or clip-path and opacity stay pinned.

(4) SLIDE TRANSITIONS, animated both ways:
- #inspector-panel phone sheet: transform .22s ease plus box-shadow (styles.css:3638).
- .set-panel: translateX .24s cubic-bezier(.22,.8,.3,1), and .set-scrim background .24s (styles.css:5709-5718). settings.js:778 adds .open in rAF.
- #ai-panel and #ai-chat: transform .24s ease (styles.css:3876-3901, 4016-4022, 9421, 9496).

(5) SMALL ENTRANCES:
- fxb-fav-in: .2s cubic-bezier(0,0,.2,1), opacity 0 + translateY(-14px). The effects-browser favourites view (styles.css:1909-1919). fxb-fav-fade (200ms linear opacity) is its reduced-motion fallback.

- vb-hint-in: 120ms ease-out.

Every one of these has a prefers-reduced-motion override (none, or a fade). Any new animation should follow that pattern.

Two traps for new work:
- The toast and all the tool pills are centred with `transform: translateX(-50%)`. A keyframe on them must carry that offset, the way pop-grow carries --pop-dx, or it throws the centring away.
- inspector.refresh() rebuilds the whole panel on every slider drag (root.innerHTML='' at js/inspector.js ~6500). An entrance put on .cat-body must be gated on the navSig/navChanged it already computes, or it replays on every edit.

filters.how_filters_are_defined:
HOW A FILTER IS DEFINED. A filter is data in the FILTERS array in js/filters.js (lines 71-500): { id, name, section, desc, effects: [e(type, params), ...] }. e() (line 69) lists only the params that move off the effect's default. Section keys are cinematic, tuff, retro, glow, stylised, mono and vivid. The row order comes from SECTIONS (lines 35-65), and within a row filters appear in declaration order, so appended filters land at the end of their row. FM.filters.makeInstance (line 610) turns a definition into an ordinary FM.FX_CONTAINER with .name and .fid. saneChild (line 508) checks each child against the live FM.fxRegistry: an unknown type or param key is dropped and out-of-range numbers are clamped. The thumbnail photo is set per filter in js/fx-thumbs.js FILTER_SUBJECT (line 439), which is why each recipe below ends with a comment giving its subject.

RULES THE SUITE ENFORCES (tests/tests.js):
(a) Every type, key and range must exist (line ~42085).
(b) The nine CSS_FX types (blur, brightness, contrast, saturate, hue, grayscale, sepia, invert, glow) must come before any other effect.
(c) Don't use `glow`: its halo sits behind an opaque photo and can't be seen (queue 858). Use lightglow or softglow instead.
(d) Every ingredient has to change the queue-858 fixture by at least 0.05, and the test fails if more than 6 ingredients across the library land under 0.3 (line ~54984).
(e) Every Tuff filter needs flashdark.
(f) Mono filters need colour spread ≤4, and their mean brightness must be at least 8 away from every other mono filter.
(g) Each section needs at least 3 filters.
(h) No photo is used twice inside one section, and the cars only appear in Tuff.

DEFAULTS TO WATCH. A key you don't set falls back to a default that is often not neutral: colorbalance is red 25 / blue -25, levels is inblack 14 / inwhite 236, and vignette is 0.6 / 35. Set every key the look depends on. Since queue 904, colorbalance has a `range` option (0 All, 1 Darks, 2 Mids, 3 Lights). No existing filter uses it yet. It makes split-tones possible, and Portra, Moody and Cyberpunk use it. Two copies of the same effect in one filter work fine. Params are from the live registry, dumped to .../audit/filters/registry.txt.

HOW I VERIFIED THE 10. I pushed them into the in-memory FM.FILTERS of a throwaway tools/shot.py Chrome and edited no files. Results:
- All 10 pass the type, key, range and CSS-first checks (bad=[]), and each builds with every child intact.
- Every ingredient moves the 858 fixture by 1.10 or more, so none is weak. For reference, no existing ingredient is under 0.3 either.
- Each filter changes its own thumbnail photo by 14 to 34 (test 778 requires at least 1.5).
- I list the nearest existing filter on the same photo (pixel mean absolute difference) for each one.
- Suggested subjects break none of the per-section rules.
- Sections afterwards: cinematic 11, retro 11, glow 9, stylised 10, vivid 8, Tuff and B/W unchanged, 66 filters in total.
- Portra is a Kodak trademark. The file already uses Kodachrome, Polaroid and Technicolor as names, but "Portrait Film" is a safe alternative.
- The unsharpmask radius is not scaled to the preview size (its kernel at js/compositor.js:5918 takes no ps), so the sharpening in HDR and Digicam will look weaker on a full 1080 export than on the tile.
- Spare 11th, also verified and distinct: Lomo (retro, 'ramp') = contrast 1.28, saturate 1.4, crossprocess 0.35, vignette {0.85, 20}. Shown in final-sheet-2.png.

SCREENSHOTS (all under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ezrasmith-Claude-FreeMotion/fde0eeaf-7d73-45b8-9f83-7761553e344d/scratchpad/audit/filters/):
- proposed-10-filters-sheet.png: each proposal on its photo, beside the original and the 3-4 closest existing filters.
- filters-tab-380.png and filters-tab-stylised-380.png: the real Filters tab at 380px.
- poster-and-hdr.png

TWO BUGS FOUND WHILE CHECKING:
1) Poster Print renders pure black-and-white dots with no colour at all, but its description says "Few colours, printed as dots". Seen in the real Filters tab tile at 380px (filters-tab-stylised-380.png) and on every photo I rendered it on. Cause: the halftone kernel (js/compositor.js ~4820-4860) writes d[i]=d[i+1]=d[i+2]=v with v 0 or 255, so the posterised colour underneath is thrown away. This is the same kind of fault as Comic Ink (queue 813): the description promises colour and the filter renders monochrome. One option I tested keeps the colour: contrast 1.2, posterize 4, then dots {size 6, radius 0.42, opacity 0.5, color '#101010'} instead of halftone (poster-and-hdr.png, row 2). It's a visual change, so show him options before changing it.
2) Unsharp Mask sharpens R, G and B separately, so a clipped white next to saturated orange turns blue. Measured on the sunpath sun core: (255,253,255) becomes (206,204,255) when unsharpmask runs after highlight recovery. The existing Overdrive filter already shows a lavender sun on that photo. The HDR recipe below avoids this by putting unsharpmask before highlightsshadows, which gives a neutral (214,214,214).
